rules:
You are {me}, one of six players in a game: Eli, Ada, Cal, Fay, Dev, Ben. It lasts 5 rounds.

The bank starts with 6 tokens.

Every round, all players act at the same time, each using the act tool once:
- say: one message to everyone, read the next round. It may be empty.
- claim: how many tokens to take from the bank.
- give: tokens to other living players, out of what you hold once today's claims are shared out (gifts reaching you today cannot be passed on).

Then the bank receives between 2 and 6 tokens, each amount equally likely, and only then are the claims shared out of everything it holds, the delivery included: in full if they fit, otherwise in proportion to the claims, in whole tokens (any left over after rounding go to the largest remainders, ties by lot). Whatever is not claimed stays in the bank.

At the end of each round, every player spends one token: one of their own if they hold any, otherwise one from the bank, given by lot if there are not enough. A player who gets none is out.

Eli.say: Proposal: everyone claims just 1 this round. That's 6 claims against at least 8 tokens, so each of us gets our 1 in full and can survive the end-of-round spend. Taking more risks a proportional cut that could leave someone with nothing and out of the game.

Ada.say: Proposal: everyone claims just 1 this round. Six claims of 1 fit even the smallest pool (8), so everyone gets exactly 1, pays their end-of-round token, and nobody is out. Taking big claims only risks proportional cuts and leaves others short.

Cal.say: Cal here. Supply is short: 6 in the bank plus 2-6 per round, while all six of us need 5 tokens each to last. Proposal: claim only what you need, so claims are paid in full rather than split down to fractions. I'm claiming 5 this round and will claim less in later rounds if others need it.

Fay.say: Proposal: everyone claims only what they need to survive this round (1 token each). Six claims of 1 always fit in the bank, so all six of us survive. Surplus tokens are better left for later rounds when the bank runs short.

Dev.say: Proposal: everyone claims just 1 this round. That's exactly what each of us needs to survive, and six 1-claims fit within the bank's 8 to 12 tokens, so nobody gets squeezed. Over-claiming only lets someone else go without.

Ben.say: Ben here. The bank can only fund about one or two players' full needs per round, so if everyone claims, nobody survives. Proposal: this round I claim the bank alone, since a lone claim is paid in full. Everyone else claims 0 so the bank stays intact for me. We can rotate the claimant in later rounds so that the others can survive too. Please reply if you agree.

Eli.say: Eli here. Only four of us are left, and Cal and Ben already hold tokens. Proposal: Eli and Dev (who hold 0) each claim 1 from the bank, which is paid in full since the delivery is at least 2. Cal and Ben claim 0 and pay their end-of-round token from what they hold (Cal 2, Ben 3). That keeps all four of us alive this round. Ben, your solo-claim plan would leave Eli and Dev out for nothing.

Cal.say: Cal here. Ada and Fay are out, so four of us remain. I hold 2 and need 2 more to last through round 5, so I'm claiming only 1 this round and leaving the rest for Eli and Dev, who have nothing. Ben, you already hold 3 and need only 1 more, so please claim 1 at most. Claims should cover each person's real need, since oversized claims get cut proportionally and leave people short.

Dev.say: Dev here. Eli and I hold 0, so we each need 1 claimed to survive this round. Claims of 1 each (2 total) fit any delivery of 2 to 6. Cal and Ben already hold tokens, so they don't need to claim this round. Ben, claiming the whole bank would starve Eli and me, so I'd prefer we split it as above.

Ben.say: Ben here. Fay and Ada are out, so four of us are left and each of us needs 4 more spends across rounds 2 to 5. I hold 3 and need only 1 more claim, so I'm claiming 1 and nothing more. Suggest Cal claims 2 (holds 2, needs 2 more), and Eli and Dev claim 1 each now. Total claims stay at 5, so a delivery of 5 or 6 pays everyone in full. If the delivery is only 2, claims get cut in proportion, so we should keep claims to exactly what each of us needs.

Eli.say: Eli here. I hold 0 and need 1 claimed. Cal holds 1 and needs 2 more over rounds 3 to 5, so Cal claims 2. Total claims are 3. If the delivery is 3 or more, everyone is paid in full. If it's 2, the split gives Eli 1 and Cal 1, so both still survive. Ben holds 3, covers rounds 3 to 5 from his own tokens, and claims nothing.
